Work & learning

Experience

Engineering in Guangzhou, computer science in Toronto, and a few classrooms along the way.

Jul–Aug 2026 / GuangzhouAI & Cloud Solutions Engineering InternAspire Digital Technology, Guangzhou Branch

At Aspire Digital Technology (Shenzhen), Guangzhou Branch, I led the Rokid exhibition-guide project and worked across agent evaluation and user-facing features.

  • Integrated the Android camera pipeline with a Python recognition service and helped keep exhibit context current.
  • Evaluated AI agents on search, tool use and scheduled tasks, documenting failures I could reproduce.
  • Worked on task feedback and exception alerts across web and mini-program features.

Device integration & debugging

I worked with He Yutong on recognition, knowledge-based answers, HUD subtitles and speech. My work crossed BLE initialization, Socket authentication, MediaCodec frame decoding, Kotlin, FastAPI and Dify. One connection bug required tracing asynchronous callbacks and state flags across the device handshake rather than changing the recognition model.

Release discipline

After recognition and introduction were accepted, we preserved that baseline while extending dialogue. I kept software regression results separate from hardware demonstrations and the manual checks still outstanding at handoff. When model-service failures leaked operational text into subtitles, I separated fallback logs from visitor-facing answers.

Research & communication

Alongside the device project, I investigated whether an agent should use, ignore or ask about a stored memory. I prepared a talk on agent-memory reliability and practised explaining evidence, context and authorization boundaries to an audience beyond the implementation team.

Expected Apr 2029 / TorontoHonours BSc, Computer ScienceUniversity of Toronto, St. George

I'm completing an Honours BSc in Computer Science, with an expected graduation in April 2029. My project work spans browser agents, connected devices and memory-use research.

What I'm studying

Current coursework includes Java software design and object-oriented programming, proofs and computational reasoning, multivariable calculus, and probability. Linear algebra provides another foundation for my machine-learning work. These are studies in progress, not a claim that I have completed an AI or systems specialization.

Work outside class

AllAbout Campus turns a familiar student problem—finding the relevant course rule—into a browser-agent and evidence-routing project. My independent Memory Guard work asks a different question: when should previously stored information change today's recommendation?

Sep–Dec 2024 / Xinshao, ChinaVolunteer AI teachingRural students in Xinshao

I taught what a computer is, classification and simple neural networks. When the classroom had no computer for the slides I'd brought, I explained machine learning with a Peppa Pig robot story instead.

That experience still shapes how I explain technical work: the explanation has to fit the room.

Teaching without the planned tools

The lesson started with what a computer is, then moved to classification and simple neural networks. Without a computer to show the slides, I used the robot story to make the ideas accessible. The concrete challenge was translating unfamiliar technical language into something students could follow with the resources in the classroom.

2024 / Summer programData analysis & machine learningJohns Hopkins summer program

Before university, I analysed obesity risk factors using Python and XGBoost in a Johns Hopkins summer program.

Project focus

The project studied obesity risk factors through a Python-based machine-learning analysis using XGBoost. It was educational data analysis, not a clinical diagnostic tool or evidence of a causal relationship.

Place in my work

This is the earliest machine-learning project in this portfolio. The later cases show the shift toward building complete systems: browser evidence collection, connected-device interactions and explicit review of uncertain information.
